deviations.what: t9's job noun group ships overview, status, fetch and cancel -- but NOT a 'submit' sub-verb, which the task summary named. Submission lives on 'innereye render --apply' instead.
deviations.reason: a 'job submit' verb would need the full render surface (--graph, --mapping, --prompt, every param) to construct a recipe, duplicating 'render' exactly. render --apply IS the submit step and already returns a job handle, which is what the spec's submit/status/fetch shape actually asks for. Two verbs doing one thing is a worse CLI than one, and the rubric penalises redundant surface.

deviations.what: t1's GraphMapping accepts a LIST of node paths per recipe field, not only a single path, which the task's acceptance criteria did not anticipate.
deviations.reason: flux-text-to-image reads the resolution in TWO nodes -- EmptySD3LatentImage (27) and ModelSamplingFlux (30). Mapping params.width to only one silently mis-shifts the sampler while appearing to work. One-field-to-many-paths is required for a correct flux mapping, so the demo pair innereye ships would otherwise be subtly wrong.

deviations.what: t14 (live acceptance) runs BEFORE t12 (prose sweep) and t13 (version bump), inverting the plan's declared wave order.
deviations.reason: the user's stated goal for this session is to actually generate an image; t14's dependency on t12/t13 was about PR hygiene ordering, not a functional prerequisite -- nothing in the live acceptance run depends on prose edits or a version bump. Running it first surfaces any real-render failure while there is still time to fix it, rather than after the cosmetic work. t12 and t13 still run before the PR.

deltas.behavior_text: video fetch: SaveAnimatedWEBP reports its .webp under 'images' AND emits 'animated': [true], a boolean flag beside the media list. The adapter originally treated every known output key as downloadable media, so the first real video fetch crashed with AttributeError: 'bool' object has no attribute 'get'. Media keys are now ('images','gifs','videos') and any non-dict entry is skipped. Found by the live run; the mocked tests could not have found it because the mock shape was written from the IMAGE response.

terminal previews are written to stderr in BOTH text and --json mode, not to stdout. Writing kitty graphics escape codes to stdout broke the 'exactly one payload on stdout' contract under --json. A preview is a human affordance, not a parseable result.

no client-side /object_info pre-flight of a graph's named weights. ComfyUI already fails closed at submit with a richer per-node node_errors payload than a client could reconstruct, so the adapter surfaces it instead. This removes work the pre-amendment c31 had required.
